proof.criterion: Criterion 1 - a reader who opens an issue's Conversation sees one card per conversation, no event line appears in it, and the issue's whole event history is on a new Activity tab at /issues/<KEY>/activity.
proof.surface: CI job `dispatch` (workflow "Legion Envoy and Contracts"): the repository's Playwright suite in four browser projects, driving the built dashboard against the real Go Dispatch server and a pgvector/pgvector Postgres with the real migrations. The suite cannot run in a Legion worker pod - no container runtime, no Postgres, no pgvector - so this is the production-like surface the plan names.
proof.observed: success. On an issue seeded with two asks (one answered, one retracted), two comment threads (one resolved), one message thread and status, claim and document-version events, the Conversation draws exactly 5 `li[data-turn]` inside `ol[aria-label="Conversation turns"]` and 0 elements matching `[data-kind="activity"]`, while /issues/<KEY>/activity lists at least 3 event rows in `ol[aria-label="Issue activity"]` - the rows the Conversation does not draw. The tab keeps five labelled tabs with Activity last, `t v` selects it and the `?` help list shows its row, and an uploaded document's line is an Activity row and nothing else.
proof.negativeControl: e2e/activity.e2e.ts is the one-card check's own control: the same seed must draw `updated the issue`, `claimed the issue` and `added note.md` as exactly one Activity row each, with no Conversation list and no `[data-turn]` mounted on that route. If the split had not happened, one of the two halves necessarily fails.

proof.criterion: Criterion 2 - a link to a conversation lands on it, marked; a reply written under an ask and a retracted ask land for the first time, and a reply in a resolved comment thread keeps landing.
proof.surface: The same CI job `dispatch`, case e2e/deep-links.e2e.ts "every item link lands on exactly one marked card, and a reply link marks its row too", in all four browser projects.
proof.observed: success. Navigating the item path for a reply written under an ask, for a retracted ask, for a reply in a resolved comment thread and for the href a search hit carries each leaves exactly one `li[data-turn][aria-current="true"]` in the turns list, and for the two reply cases exactly one marked `[data-reply][aria-current="true"]` row - inside the card above the phone breakpoint, inside the full-screen Thread dialog below it, where the Conversation deliberately marks the list `aria-hidden`/`inert` while a thread covers it.
proof.negativeControl: The same case keeps both of its existing controls: a comment id that belongs to another issue still redirects to that issue's path rather than marking anything here, and a made-up uuid still renders the `Comment not found` page.

proof.criterion: Criterion 3 - the conversations are listed newest reply first with All, Open and Closed filters that start on All and are not carried over from an earlier visit; the Show activity, Show retracted and Resolved (N) controls go, and the settings a browser already stores for them change nothing.
proof.surface: The same CI job `dispatch`, cases in e2e/conversation.e2e.ts and e2e/threads.e2e.ts.
proof.observed: success. In a browser context that has never visited Dispatch the filter reads All and an answered ask, a retracted ask and a resolved comment thread are each visible; in a context seeded through addInitScript with dispatch.conversation.showActivity=false and dispatch.conversation.showRetracted=false the same three are visible, so the stored settings change nothing. Switching to Open hides the answered ask and switching back to All shows it. An ask answered after a later comment thread sorts above it. On an issue of more than 200 events whose oldest conversation is a closed ask, that ask is listed under Closed with no `Load older` click - the defect this change exists to fix. The margin suites pass with their own `Resolved (N)` and retracted-fold assertions unmodified.
proof.negativeControl: Switching the filter to Open must hide the answered ask, and switching back to All must show it again, in the same case - so a filter that silently showed everything would fail rather than pass.

trickyParts: The list had to stop being event-derived. Every card used to come from GET /issues/{key}/events read 200 at a time, so a conversation older than that window was simply absent - which the spec's own check forbids. The three per-issue entity reads replace it, and the event log is now read twice, one row each, only for the unread boundary and the issue head.

Pin identity had to change with the source. A card built from /comments or /messages has no event id at all - only an ask carries one - so a Conversation card pins under `<kind>:<id>` while an Activity row keeps pinning under `event:<id>`, and the margin's Pinned tab resolves both. Stated consequence, not migrated: a conversation pinned before this change keeps appearing in the margin as its event's line while its card shows unpinned until it is pinned again.

The unread mark is a single watermark (user_issue_state.last_read_seq) and cannot express per-conversation read state. A dwell on the newest conversation writes the issue head; dwelling lower writes nothing. The tab under-marks rather than over-marks, so an unread conversation is never hidden. Only the Conversation writes the mark; Activity renders it and writes nothing.

The Activity tab lost a thing the old tab had by accident: the old ConversationTab called useAgents twice - once gated on a claim event and once unconditionally for its composer - and the second call warmed the registry, which is how an activity line authored by a session got its title. The Activity tab has no composer, so the gate now also fires when any loaded row was written by a session. CI caught this; a component test pins it.

GitHub built no head for this pull request for about an hour, through two pushes and a close/reopen, because the branch had become CONFLICTING against main and GitHub computes no merge ref for a conflicting head. The fix was the forward merge, not a rebase.
